ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath.rationale: `=> false`. C# strips a dead creature's powers at CreatureCmd.cs:533; the sim never removes powers on death, so `false` is its universal behaviour and this override is satisfied for free. The inverse -- the C# default is `true` and the sim strips nothing -- is the engine-wide absence reported in content-power-report-b.md section 3c. ENGINE-LEVEL SIBLING (added 2026-07-26): the INVERSE finding -- that C#'s DEFAULT is `true` so every power WITHOUT this override should be stripped on its owner's death and in the sim none is -- now carries a verdict of its own at audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 8b (`gap`, LIVE, executed on the Decimillipede). It used to exist only as prose in content-power-report-b.md section 3c. This entry stays `faithful` because the override asks for exactly the behaviour the sim gives for free; the engine-wide absence is step 8b's, not this unit's.

ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-27. The retention observable is closed -- the sim's death-prevention arm now leaves the creature dead at 0 HP with `retained_after_death = True` (cmds.py:62) -- but this power still does not implement `should_remove_from_combat_after_death` (PainfulStabsPower.cs:28-32), because AdaptablePower on the same creature reaches retention by the prevention arm. Folded into power/adaptable's AfterDeath mechanism. DORMANT, RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30 by enumerating PainfulStabsPower's sole applier: Test Subject is the ONLY ported source (sts2_rl/monsters/glory/test_subject.py). `AdaptablePower` is applied unconditionally in `__init__` (:59-61) and PainfulStabsPower is only ever applied inside `_respawn` at `self._respawns == 1` (:130-136), i.e. it never exists on Test Subject without Adaptable already present. Both are removed TOGETHER at `self._respawns == 2` (:140-141, entering the final phase 3, where the third death is real and no prevention/retention applies at all). So there is no point in Test Subject's lifecycle where PainfulStabsPower is present and AdaptablePower is not -- the retention question is always answered by Adaptable's own (already-live, see power/_death_prevention_branch) AfterDeath mechanism before this power's absent override could matter. No other ported applier exists to widen this.

AfterAttack.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-27, and a NEW residual is recorded. THE HOOK IS FIXED: PainfulStabsPower now implements `after_attack(dealer, card, results)` (powers.py:3927-3946), groups the AttackCommand results by player receiver and adds `Amount * hits` Wounds once per receiver, matching PainfulStabsPower.cs:34-68; `hooks.after_attack` supplies the results (hooks.py:829-841). Divergence (a), the killing blow, and (b), the mid-attack timing, are both gone. WHAT REMAINS: PainfulStabsPower.cs:36's third early-return condition, `!command.DamageProps.IsPoweredAttack()`, is not expressed -- the sim's attack bracket carries no props and powers.py:3933-3939 tests only the dealer and the receiver's side. DORMANT, RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30: `hooks.before_attack`/`hooks.after_attack` (hooks.py:812-841) take only `(dealer, card)` / `(dealer, card, results)` -- there is no `props` parameter anywhere in the bracket's signature, for ANY caller, so no ported OR unported call site could carry an unpowered-attack signal through this hook today even if one wanted to. The only caller that reaches PainfulStabsPower's dealer role is `Monster._execute_attack` (monsters/base.py:127-138), which brackets every hit with `ctx.hooks.before_attack(self)` / `after_attack(self)` and no props concept at all -- every monster attack is implicitly 'powered' in the sim's model. NOTE this record's guard on 'the three AfterAttack early-return conditions' is corrected to match below (folded, same mechanism, same verdict).

guards.issue: RE-OPENED 2026-07-28. Two of the three early-return conditions map; the THIRD does not, and the AfterAttack hook entry in this record already says so ("NOTE this record's guard on 'the three AfterAttack early-return conditions' still reads `faithful`, which is no longer true of the third one") -- the re-derivation pass wrote that sentence and left this entry at `faithful` anyway. PainfulStabsPower.cs:36 is `command.Attacker != base.Owner || command.TargetSide == base.Owner.Side || !command.DamageProps.IsPoweredAttack()`. The sim's after_attack bracket carries no props at all -- `def after_attack(self, dealer, card=None)` (hooks.py:829-841), which passes only (dealer, card, results) to listeners -- and powers.py:3933-3939 tests only `dealer is not self.owner` and, per result, `receiver.side != "player"`. So the IsPoweredAttack test has no expression anywhere on this path. DORMANT, RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30: `hooks.before_attack`/`after_attack` (hooks.py:812-841) carry no `props` parameter for any caller, and `Monster._execute_attack` (monsters/base.py:127-138), the sole dealer-side path that reaches this power, brackets every hit with no props concept at all -- there is no ported or unported call site today that could express an unpowered attack through this bracket. Folded with the AfterAttack entry's residual: one mechanism, one verdict (both `live: false`). CITATION FIX: the old rationale cited powers.py:3400-3405 for the props test; after the powers.py reshuffle those lines are inside HexPower, and the code they described no longer exists at that location -- corrected here to powers.py:3933-3939. The two conditions that DO map: `command.Attacker != base.Owner` -> `dealer is not self.owner`, and `command.TargetSide == base.Owner.Side` -> the per-receiver `receiver.side != "player"` filter, which is equivalent for a single-player enemy owner.
